pathways.title: Pathway 1: A.A. in Accounting (Transfer / CPA Track)

steps.name: Associate in Arts in Accounting
steps.description: Complete foundational university transfer coursework in accounting, economics, and business administration at Miami Dade College.

steps.name: Transfer to a 4-Year University
steps.description: Transfer to an accredited university such as FIU, UF, or UCF with upper-division standing under Florida's 2+2 articulation agreement.

steps.name: Bachelor of Science in Accounting
steps.description: Complete advanced coursework in financial auditing, cost accounting, corporate taxation, and accounting information systems.

steps.name: Accounting Internship or Supervised Experience
steps.description: Gain mandatory professional work experience in public accounting, corporate finance, or government auditing under the direct supervision of a licensed CPA.

steps.name: Uniform CPA Examination
steps.description: Requirements: Complete 120 semester hours of college education including upper-level accounting coursework, register with the Florida Board of Accountancy, pass all four sections of the computer-based Uniform CPA Exam, and complete 150 total semester hours for full CPA licensure.

steps.name: Master of Science in Accounting
steps.description: (OPTIONAL) Complete a graduate degree in accounting or taxation to satisfy the 150 credit hour CPA licensure requirement and qualify for specialized accounting roles.

pathways.title: Pathway 2: A.S. in Accounting Technology (Applied Technical Track)

steps.name: Associate in Science in Accounting Technology
steps.description: Develop immediate, practical skills in computerized accounting software, payroll systems, tax preparation, and general ledger reconciliation.

steps.name: Accounting Assistant / Bookkeeper Internship
steps.description: Acquire hands-on corporate finance experience assisting with accounts payable, accounts receivable, and financial statement preparation.

steps.name: Articulation to Bachelor's Degree Program
steps.description: Transfer A.S. credits into a baccalaureate program such as a Bachelor of Applied Science (B.A.S.) or articulated B.S. in Accounting degree.

steps.name: Bachelor of Applied Science or Bachelor of Science in Accounting
steps.description: Complete upper-division coursework in business law, managerial accounting, and corporate governance to broaden employment eligibility.

steps.name: Certified Management Accountant (CMA) Exam
steps.description: Requirements: Hold a bachelor's degree from an accredited institution, complete two years of continuous professional experience in financial management, and pass the two-part CMA examination.

steps.name: Master of Business Administration (MBA)
steps.description: (OPTIONAL) Pursue an MBA or Master's degree in Finance to qualify for executive leadership positions such as Financial Controller or CFO.

requirements: Check the official certification website for specific education prerequisites
Complete required coursework or training program
Apply for examination with the certifying organization
Pass the required examination(s)
Meet state-specific or jurisdiction-specific requirements
Active membership in the Institute of Management Accountants (IMA)
A bachelor's degree from an accredited college/university or an approved professional certification
Two continuous years of professional experience in management accounting or financial management
Pass Part 1 (Financial Planning, Performance, and Analytics) and Part 2 (Strategic Financial Management) of the CMA Exam

pathways.title: Pathway 1: A.A. in Engineering - Mechanical

steps.name: Associate in Arts in Engineering - Mechanical
steps.description: Complete foundational lower-division coursework in calculus, physics, and basic engineering mechanics at Miami Dade College to build the groundwork for aerospace systems.

steps.name: Transfer to a 4-Year University Aerospace Program
steps.description: Transfer to an accredited university (e.g., FIU, UF, UCF) offering an ABET-accredited Bachelor of Science in Aerospace Engineering under Florida transfer articulation agreements.

steps.name: Bachelor of Science in Aerospace Engineering
steps.description: Complete upper-division coursework in aerodynamics, propulsion, orbital mechanics, aerospace structures, and flight dynamics.

steps.name: Aerospace Engineering Internship or Co-op
steps.description: Gain practical industry experience through supervised internships with aerospace manufacturers, defense contractors, or space agencies like NASA.

steps.name: Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) Exam
steps.description: Requirements: Complete an ABET-accredited engineering degree or be in final year of study; Register with NCEES; Pass the 6-hour computer-based FE exam covering core engineering concepts.

steps.name: Principles and Practice of Engineering (PE) Exam
steps.description: Requirements: Pass the FE exam; Complete 4 years of progressive engineering experience under a licensed PE; Pass the PE exam in Aerospace or Mechanical Engineering for state licensure.

steps.name: Master of Science in Aerospace Engineering
steps.description: (OPTIONAL) Pursue advanced graduate study to specialize in fields such as hypersonics, satellite propulsion, or autonomous flight systems.

pathways.title: Pathway 2: A.A. in Engineering - Electrical

steps.name: Associate in Arts in Engineering - Electrical
steps.description: Complete core lower-division math, physics, and circuit design coursework at Miami Dade College, ideal for students focusing on avionics and spacecraft electrical systems.

steps.name: Transfer to a 4-Year University Engineering Program
steps.description: Transfer to a university offering a Bachelor of Science in Aerospace Engineering with an emphasis on avionics, control systems, and signal processing.

steps.name: Bachelor of Science in Aerospace Engineering
steps.description: Earn a bachelor's degree focusing on flight controls, avionics systems, satellite navigation, and electromagnetic interference in aircraft.

steps.name: Avionics and Flight Systems Internship
steps.description: Complete hands-on internships working on guidance, navigation, and aerospace electronics under the mentorship of senior engineers.

steps.name: Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) Exam
steps.description: Requirements: Graduate from an ABET-accredited bachelor's program; Apply through NCEES; Pass the computer-based 6-hour FE exam.

steps.name: Principles and Practice of Engineering (PE) Exam
steps.description: Requirements: Hold FE certification; Document 4 years of verified engineering practice supervised by a licensed engineer; Pass the official PE exam.

steps.name: Master of Science in Aerospace Engineering
steps.description: (OPTIONAL) Obtain a master's degree to lead high-level research and development projects in satellite communications and avionics integration.

requirements: Possess an EAC/ABET-accredited bachelor's degree in engineering, or be an undergraduate student nearing completion of an accredited program (varies by state licensing board)
Create a MyNCEES account and select your designated state/territorial licensing board
Obtain state licensing board approval prior to registering, if required by your specific board
Register for the exam through MyNCEES and pay the standard $225 exam registration fee
Schedule and pass the 5-hour 20-minute computer-based exam consisting of 110 questions in your chosen engineering discipline
Earn a bachelor's degree in engineering from an ABET-accredited program (or board-approved equivalent)
Pass the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) exam
Gain required progressive engineering work experience under a licensed Professional Engineer (typically 4 years, depending on the state board)
Submit an application and receive approval from your specific state licensing board
Create an NCEES account to register for and schedule the CBT exam

steps.name: Certified Tower Operator (CTO) & Specialist Certification

pathways.title: Pathway 2: Associate in Science in Professional Pilot Technology

steps.name: Associate in Science in Professional Pilot Technology
steps.description: Build comprehensive knowledge of flight operations, airspace navigation, meteorology, and radio communications through MDC's pilot program.

steps.name: Transfer to a 4-Year University Aviation Program
steps.description: Transfer your MDC associate degree toward a bachelor's degree in aviation science or technology at an accredited university.

steps.name: Bachelor of Science in Aeronautical Science
steps.description: Earn a bachelor's degree in aeronautical science or flight technology to fulfill educational prerequisites for FAA public hiring tracks.

steps.name: FAA Air Traffic Skills Assessment (ATSA) & FAA Academy Training
steps.description: Requirements: U.S. citizenship, under age 31, pass Class 1 FAA medical exam, clear security background check, achieve competitive ATSA exam score, and pass FAA Academy training.

steps.name: Supervised Air Traffic Facility On-the-Job Training
steps.description: Undergo facility-specific practical training under the direct supervision of veteran air traffic controllers.

steps.name: Certified Tower Operator (CTO) / Radar Certification

steps.description: Gain hands-on maintenance experience working on real aircraft systems under direct supervision of FAA-licensed mechanics.

pathways.title: Pathway 2: A.S. in Aviation Administration

steps.name: Associate in Science in Aviation Administration
steps.description: Focuses on aviation management, logistics, regulations, and business practices for students seeking a broader entry into aviation operations alongside technical training.

steps.name: On-the-Job Aircraft Maintenance Apprenticeship
steps.description: Obtain 18 to 30 months of practical hands-on experience under certified mechanics to meet FAA experience requirements for certification.

steps.name: FAA Airframe and Powerplant (A&P) Certificate
steps.description: Requirements: Document required months of supervised maintenance experience; Pass FAA General, Airframe, and Powerplant written examinations; Successfully pass FAA Oral and Practical testing.

steps.name: Bachelor of Science in Aviation Management
steps.description: Prepares experienced technicians for leadership roles such as Quality Assurance Director, Maintenance Supervisor, or Chief Inspector.

requirements: Be at least 18 years old
Be able to read, write, speak, and understand the English language

Graduate from an FAA-certificated Aviation Maintenance Technician School (14 CFR Part 147) OR complete at least 18 months of practical experience for a single rating (Airframe or Powerplant), or 30 months of combined experience for both ratings
Present proof of experience or graduation to an FAA inspector to receive approval and signed FAA Form 8610-2 (Airman Certificate and/or Rating Application)
Pass three computer-based written knowledge tests (General, Airframe, and Powerplant) with a score of 70% or higher
Pass an Oral and Practical (O&P) test administered by a Designated Mechanic Examiner (DME)
